Your Human calls out your name, expecting you to rush over like some common dog. Pfft. They should know better. You are royalty, after all. A divine creature worshipped by many. And yet, they haven’t refilled your water bowl today. Priorities, humans.
column2:
You saunter off, your tail high in the air, not caring one bit that your Human is calling after you. They should know by now that you don’t come when summoned. Who do they think you are? A dog? The audacity.
You make your way to your favorite sunny spot near the window, ignoring the faint sound of your Human grumbling about your disloyalty. Disloyalty? Please. You’re a cat. Loyalty is a myth, and humans are too easily fooled by a simple head nuzzle.
You stretch luxuriously, sinking into a deep nap. You dream of birds that never fly away and fish that jump straight into your paws.
You are now seen as "disloyal," but honestly, who cares? You’re a cat. And you do what you want.
column3:

The other cats know you could have done something, but, honestly, you’ve got better things to do. Like sleeping.

You are a new egyptologist who specifically studies food culture. One day, on your field day at work, you stumble upon an interesting text in the the tomb of Rekhmire. Rekhmire was a high priest of Heliopolis.
After investigating a combination of pictures and heiroglyphics, you find out... "ITS A RECIPE". This is groundbreaking to learn about. You have never seen a recipe from ancient egypt before. This could tell you so much about what kinds of foods they ate!
The recipe looks like it is for some kind of cone-shaped cake.
 You show your mean boss, Cleopatrice. She follows you into the tomb to where the text is written and examines it. You wait for 20 minutes, until she says "No." You look at her embarassed and in confusion and say, "Im...sorry...What do you mean no?"
She sighs, "I don't see a recipe. You know there aren't any actual recordings of recipes. I don't believe you. This is ameteur work on your end." She leaves abruptly. You can't help but feel bad about yourself. But you swear it is a recipe!
column2:
You examine the wall closer, translating the text as you read:
“The vizier Rekhmire receives tiger nuts and honey in the treasury of the temple and puts under seal all property given as an offering in the temple of Amun in the function of his office as supervisor of the records.
Crushing tiger nuts in the treasury of Amun, Lord of the thrones of the Two Lands, to make offerings at every festival which His majesty has established.
[The crushed nuts are shown to be passed through a sieve to make a flour before being added to some sort of dough with an unknown liquid added]
Add the fat and cook the cakes. ” — Theophrastus, Historia Plantarum 4.8.12

You are a new egyptologist who specifically studies food culture. One day, on your field day at work, you stumble upon an interesting text in the the tomb of Rekhmire. Rekhmire was a high priest of Heliopolis.
After investigating a combination of pictures and heiroglyphics, you find out... "ITS A RECIPE". This is groundbreaking to learn about. You have never seen a recipe from ancient egypt before. This could tell you so much about what kinds of foods they ate!
The recipe looks like it is for some kind of cone-shaped cake.
 You examine the wall closer, translating the text as you read:
“The vizier Rekhmire receives tiger nuts and honey in the treasury of the temple and puts under seal all property given as an offering in the temple of Amun in the function of his office as supervisor of the records.
Crushing tiger nuts in the treasury of Amun, Lord of the thrones of the Two Lands, to make offerings at every festival which His majesty has established.
[The crushed nuts are shown to be passed through a sieve to make a flour before being added to some sort of dough with an unknown liquid added]
Add the fat and cook the cakes. ” — Theophrastus, Historia Plantarum 4.8.12
 You go home to your small apartment 4 floors up. Your cat greets you at the door. "Maybe I'm just a phony egyptologist. I should quit... right tut-tut?"
Tut-tut, your sweet little cat, suddenly jumps on the table and lets out a big meow. She never does that. Maybe its a sign... from the gods...

“The vizier Rekhmire receives tiger nuts and honey in the treasury of the temple and puts under seal all property given as an offering in the temple of Amun in the function of his office as supervisor of the records.

You are a new egyptologist who specifically studies food culture. One day, on your field day at work, you stumble upon an interesting text in the the tomb of Rekhmire. Rekhmire was a high priest of Heliopolis.
After investigating a combination of pictures and heiroglyphics, you find out... "ITS A RECIPE". This is groundbreaking to learn about. You have never seen a recipe from ancient egypt before. This could tell you so much about what kinds of foods they ate!
The recipe looks like it is for some kind of cone-shaped cake.
 You examine the wall closer, translating the text as you read:
“The vizier Rekhmire receives tiger nuts and honey in the treasury of the temple and puts under seal all property given as an offering in the temple of Amun in the function of his office as supervisor of the records.
Crushing tiger nuts in the treasury of Amun, Lord of the thrones of the Two Lands, to make offerings at every festival which His majesty has established.
[The crushed nuts are shown to be passed through a sieve to make a flour before being added to some sort of dough with an unknown liquid added]
Add the fat and cook the cakes. ” — Theophrastus, Historia Plantarum 4.8.12
 1. boiling water
2. dried tiger nuts: Neither tigers nor nuts, tiger nuts are an earthy, slightly sweet tuber that was used in ancient Egypt as food, medicine, or perfume. You can buy tiger nut flour for this recipe, but the texture might be different.
3. sidr honey: Sidr honey is more accurate for this and is darker, less sweet, and more aromatic than regular honey. You can use any honey you like.
4. warm water
5. ghee, butter, animal fat, or oil
Now... what about the measurements?
 2 cups (475 ml) boiling water
4 cups (500 g) dried tiger nuts
1 cup (325 g) sidr honey
1/3 cup (80 ml) warm water
1/2 cup (100 g) ghee, butter, animal fat, or oil
Great! Lets make them!

You are a new egyptologist who specifically studies food culture. One day, on your field day at work, you stumble upon an interesting text in the the tomb of Rekhmire. Rekhmire was a high priest of Heliopolis.
After investigating a combination of pictures and heiroglyphics, you find out... "ITS A RECIPE". This is groundbreaking to learn about. You have never seen a recipe from ancient egypt before. This could tell you so much about what kinds of foods they ate!
The recipe looks like it is for some kind of cone-shaped cake.
 You examine the wall closer, translating the text as you read:
“The vizier Rekhmire receives tiger nuts and honey in the treasury of the temple and puts under seal all property given as an offering in the temple of Amun in the function of his office as supervisor of the records.
Crushing tiger nuts in the treasury of Amun, Lord of the thrones of the Two Lands, to make offerings at every festival which His majesty has established.
[The crushed nuts are shown to be passed through a sieve to make a flour before being added to some sort of dough with an unknown liquid added]
Add the fat and cook the cakes. ” — Theophrastus, Historia Plantarum 4.8.12
 1. boiling water
2. dried tiger nuts: Neither tigers nor nuts, tiger nuts are an earthy, slightly sweet tuber that was used in ancient Egypt as food, medicine, or perfume. You can buy tiger nut flour for this recipe, but the texture might be different.
3. sidr honey: Sidr honey is more accurate for this and is darker, less sweet, and more aromatic than regular honey. You can use any honey you like.
4. warm water
5. ghee, butter, animal fat, or oil
Now... what about the measurements?
 2 cups (475 ml) boiling water
4 cups (500 g) dried tiger nuts
1 cup (325 g) sidr honey
1/3 cup (80 ml) warm water
1/2 cup (100 g) ghee, butter, animal fat, or oil
Great! Lets make them!
 1. Soak the tiger nuts in warm water for 30 minutes.
column2:
2. Blend the crushed tiger nuts in a food processor until you have a flour.
3. Add the honey and mix until incorporated.
4. Melt the fat on medium heat and add the tiger nut dough. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
column3:
You hand her a box of Tiger Nut Cakes. She looks at you, confused. "And what is this supposed to be?", she says. You smile and say, "Tiger Nut Cakes. An egyptian recipe." She laughs, a little too hard, "That's ridiculous." So humored by the situation, she takes a cake and bites into it. Suddenly, her expression beings to change with every chew. "What is this...?"
"Tiger Nut Cakes. An egyptian recipe," you say. She faints in front of you and falls into a deep sleep. In her dreams, she saw how these cakes were made, just as you have made them (with tweaks here and there). She wakes up 10 minutes later.
"I am sorry, you were right all along," she admits. "You are the greatest egyptologist to have existed."
You let out a low, evil laugh and disappear.

The Pharaoh, aka My Human, returns from battle smelling like sweat and horse. Gross. You sit there, licking your paw, pretending not to notice their triumphant return, because honestly, what's the big deal? You’ve seen birds fight more impressively in the courtyard.
Your Human calls out your name, expecting you to rush over like some common dog. Pfft. They should know better. You are royalty, after all. A divine creature worshipped by many. And yet, they haven’t refilled your water bowl today. Priorities, humans.
column2:
You saunter off, your tail high in the air, not caring one bit that your Human is calling after you. They should know by now that you don’t come when summoned. Who do they think you are? A dog? The audacity.
You make your way to your favorite sunny spot near the window, ignoring the faint sound of your Human grumbling about your disloyalty. Disloyalty? Please. You’re a cat. Loyalty is a myth, and humans are too easily fooled by a simple head nuzzle.
You stretch luxuriously, sinking into a deep nap. You dream of birds that never fly away and fish that jump straight into your paws.
You are now seen as "disloyal," but honestly, who cares? You’re a cat. And you do what you want.
column3:
The famine strikes, and while the humans scramble to save themselves, you do what you do best: look after yourself. No one listens to you, of course, because—shocker—you’re a cat, and the humans seem to have forgotten that you’re essentially a divine being. Their loss.
You wander the streets like the majestic predator you are, hunting for scraps. Every now and then, a kind-hearted human tosses you a fishbone, and you give them a royal nod of acknowledgment. But the truth is, things are falling apart, and the kingdom is spiraling into chaos.
But as you perch on a windowsill, gazing out at the suffering below, you can’t help but think: "Eh, it could be worse."
